Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II, EDSA cor. Mapagmahal St. Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF SECRETARY 19 February 2007 HON. JORGE M. RAMOS Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member Provincial Capitol Building Romblon, Romblon Dear Sir: This pertains to your Resolution cum query, requesting for this Department's legal opinion on whether or not Section 323 of RA 7160 (The Local Government Code) is applicable on the following set of facts: On 18 October 2005, the proposed Annual Budget for the Province of Romblon was submitted by the Governor to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan; Upon receipt, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan promptly noted that the submitted Annual Budget was defective and forthwith returned the same to the Governor with its observations; Meantime that the proposed Annual Budget was with the Governor, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan conducted its regular weekly sessions and tackled other business during those sessions; It was at this point that Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member Benj amin Irao claimed that the proceedings of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan were illegal inasmuch as the Annual Budget of the province has not been approved, as provided for under Section 328 of the Local Government Code. Hence, this query. The contention is untenable. The disputed section reads: "SEC. 323. Failure to Enact the Annual Appropriations.- In case the sanggunian concerned faits to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may bc taken up during such sessions. If the sanggunian still fails to enact such ordinance after ninety 21 7_

(90) days from the beginning Of the fiscal year, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and shaZZ remain in force and effect untit the ordinance authorizing the proposed appropriations is passed by the sanggunian concerned. Howeær, only the annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shaZZ be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith. " While not so expressly stated, the foregoing section applies only if the proposed budget is already with the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for consideration, deliberation and approval as the annual appropriation ordinance. It does not apply, as in this case, when the proposed budget is returned back to the Governor as there is virtually nothing left for the Sanggunian to consider. The rationale for this is that this section is part and parcel of a cluster of sections which deals with the procedure in the enactment of local government budgets. Section 318, 2nd paragraph, and Section 319, both of the Local Government Code, provide: "SEC. 318. Preparation of the Budget by the Local Chief Executive.- xxx The ZocaZ chief executive shall submit the executive budget to the sanggunian concerned not later than, the sixteenth (16th) of October of the current fiscal year. "SEC. 319. Legislative Authorization of the Budget.- On or before the end of the current fiscal year, the sanggunian concerned shall enact, through an ordinance, the annual budget of the Zocal government unit for the ensuing fiscal year on the basis of the estimates of income and expenditures submitted by the Zocal chief executive. Clearly, the submission of the executive budget to the Sanggunian is what sets in motion the participation of the Sanggunian in the said budget as exemplified under Sections 318 and 319 of the Local Government Code. Its return back to the Governor clearly abated the prospective application of Section 323 of the same Code. Whether the procedure taken by the Sanggunian — that of returning the executive budget or, also known as the budget proposal to the Governor — is sound or not is beyond our authority to inquire as the same would necessarily involve the exercise of adjudicative powers which is vested only unto the regular courts. What is important, however, is that its return to the Governor precluded the application of Section 323 of the Code. It is axiomatic to note that Section 323 of the Local Government Code only applies in case the Sangguniang Panlalawigan fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal iliyear such that from that time, the Sanggunian is mandated to conduct sessions *311andno other business shall be tackled except the annual budget. Along this "dine, it is recalled here that SP Member Irao branded as illegal those sessions 'åeldsubsequent to 18 October 2005, date of actual submission of the 2006

executive budget to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, which were unrelated to the enactment of the 2006 annual budget. The responsibility of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan at that particular point in ;time (October 2005), assuming they did not return the ordinance to the Governor, is clearly enshrined under Section 319 of the Local Government Code, which is to pass a legislative authorization of the budget. Hence, even if from 18 October 2005 to December 2005, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan retained the same and tackled other businesses other than the enactment of the annual appropriations ordinance, the sessions are still valid since at that point in time, there is as yet no prohibition whatsoever to refrain from taking on other business except the passage of the annual budget. In conclusion, a careful and comparative readings of Sections 318, 319 and 323, inclusive, of RA 7160 clearly reveals the legislative intent insofar as the participation of the local Sanggunian in the proposed annual budget, viz: First, after the submission of the executive budget to the Sanggunian not later than the sixteenth of October of the current fiscal year, the Sanggunian is to enact the annual appropriation ordinance for the ensuing fiscal year on or before the end of the current fiscal year. Second, if it failed to enact the annual budget at the end of the current fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, without additional remuneration for its members and not take other business until such ordinance is approved. Since the factual setting in the case at bar does not approximate the underlying conditions set forth in the second elaboration as stated, we opine that, the claims made by Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member Irao is misplaced, hence, untenable. And while we are cognizant that this issue may have been rendered moot and academic with the enactment of the budget in 2006, we still feel compelled to pass upon on the same as this is one problem which is susceptible of being resurrected from time to time if not addressed with finality. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, WE EUTO T. ANDAN R Undersecret Legal:09/La cc: Director Rolando Rafael DILG Regional rv-B Aurora Blvd., Quezon City
